name: Hardware-Assisted Projection
text:
# Hardware-Assisted Projection
## Overview
Hardware-Assisted Projection is a family of volume rendering techniques that project 3D geometric primitives (tetrahedra, polyhedra, or hexahedra) onto the 2D screen space to leverage graphics hardware for scan conversion and [compositing](#2436-compositing.md) [S1, S3, unofficial]. It solves the performance bottleneck of explicit [isosurface extraction](#30-isosurface-extraction.md) and the data transfer overhead of CPU-side sorting by performing the core rendering pipeline on the GPU [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial]. Unlike [Projected Tetrahedra](877-projected-tetrahedra.md), which requires explicit triangle generation and sorting, this family leverages hardware [acceleration](#18-acceleration.md) for depth ordering or accumulation, allowing flexible data distribution and standard polygon pipeline usage [S2][S3, unofficial].
## Shared principles
The family shares a common object-order approach where 3D cells are projected into screen space, and the resulting 2D primitives are rasterized. The core mechanism involves:
1.  **Projection**: Mapping 3D cell vertices to 2D screen coordinates using view-projection matrices.
2.  **Scan Conversion**: Rasterizing the projected cells to generate fragments or ray segments.
3.  **Compositing**: Accumulating optical properties (color, opacity, or optical thickness) per pixel.

Key shared constraints:
-   **Depth Ordering**: Most variants require depth sorting (back-to-front) to correctly composite transparent volumes using [alpha blending](#5750-alpha-blending.md) [S1, unofficial][S3, unofficial].
-   **Geometric Approximation**: Curvilinear cells must be approximated as convex polyhedra with planar faces to enable standard rasterization [S3, unofficial].
-   **Hardware Utilization**: The method offloads intersection tests and interpolation to the GPU fragment shader, reducing CPU-GPU bandwidth [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial].
## Subtopics

### [Hardware-Assisted Polyhedron Projection](1453-hardware-assisted-polyhedron-projection.md)
Projects arbitrary convex polyhedral cells to 2D, generates depth-sorted ray segments via scan conversion, and composites them using hardware acceleration. It differs from raycasting by operating in image space with object-order projection, allowing flexible data distribution on distributed-memory systems and leveraging standard polygon pipelines for scan conversion. Unlike [Projected Tetrahedra](877-projected-tetrahedra.md), which requires explicit triangle generation and sorting, this method projects cells directly as polygons and relies on hardware compositing or global sorting for depth ordering.

### [Hardware-Assisted Projected Tetrahedra](1729-hardware-assisted-projected-tetrahedra.md)
Projects tetrahedra onto the screen and rasterizes them as triangles, evaluating the volume ray integral per fragment in the fragment shader. It solves the performance bottleneck of explicit isosurface extraction and the data transfer overhead of previous hybrid methods by performing the entire rendering pipeline on the GPU in a single pass. Unlike its sibling [Projected Tetrahedra](877-projected-tetrahedra.md), which requires CPU-side sorting and triangle generation, HAPT streams sorted tetrahedra as point primitives and uses the GPU [geometry shader](#4369-geometry-shader-quads.md) to decompose them into triangles. It differs from [Tetrahedral Projection with Partial Pre-integration](1861-tetrahedral-projection-with-partial-pre-integration.md) (PTINT) by eliminating the need to read data back from the GPU, allowing rendering of volumes with several million tetrahedra that would exceed GPU memory limits.

### [Absorption-Only Radiography via Unsorted Hexahedron Projection](10255-absorption-only-radiography-via-unsorted-hexahedron-projecti.md)
Simulates X-ray radiographs for curvilinear hexahedral meshes in the absorption-only regime ($J_\nu = 0$) by accumulating optical thickness additively, thereby eliminating the need for a global back-to-front visibility sort. It differs from standard polyhedron projection methods, which typically require depth sorting to correctly composite front-to-back, by leveraging the commutative property of addition in the absorption-only recurrence relation. It builds on [Hardware-Assisted Projection](5625-hardware-assisted-projection.md) by utilizing hardware fragment shaders for accumulation but specifically addresses the geometric complexity of hexahedral cells using Max's projection method.

### Röttger 3D Texture Mapping
#### definition
- [S1, unofficial] An extension of the [projected tetrahedra](#877-projected-tetrahedra.md) algorithm for hardware-accelerated rendering of volumetric data using [3D texture mapping](#9529-3d-texture-mapping.md).
#### step
- [S1, unofficial] Linearly approximate parts of the volume integral depending on segment length by modulating vertex colors.
- [S1, unofficial] Tabulate remaining parts that depend only on textural coordinates in a 2D texture map.

## Background
The concept of hardware-assisted projection evolved from early projected tetrahedra algorithms [ST90] to leverage the increasing power of GPU rasterization pipelines. Röttger et al. [RKE00] extended projected tetrahedra for hardware-accelerated rendering using 3D texture mapping, allowing accurate volumetric data rendering [S1, unofficial]. Subsequent developments, such as [Hardware-Assisted Projected Tetrahedra](#1729-hardware-assisted-projected-tetrahedra.md) (HAPT), addressed the limitations of CPU-side sorting and data transfer by streaming sorted primitives directly to the GPU geometry shader [S2, unofficial]. The family also includes specialized variants for specific data types, such as absorption-only radiography for hexahedral meshes, which removes the sorting bottleneck by exploiting the commutative nature of optical thickness accumulation [S1, unofficial]. These methods are primarily used in interactive volume visualization of unstructured grids, where performance and memory efficiency are critical [S2, unofficial].
